title: Exploring the mtcars Dataset with R
section: Relationship between horsepower and fuel efficiency
text:
Relationship between horsepower and fuel efficiency
The scatter plot below shows the relationship between horsepower and fuel efficiency (miles per gallon).

plot(
  mtcars$hp,
  mtcars$mpg,
  xlab = "Horsepower",
  ylab = "Miles per gallon",
  pch = 19
)







Figure 1: Horsepower versus miles per gallon.

title: Exploring the mtcars Dataset with R
text:
Conclusion
In this analysis, I explored the built-in mtcars dataset using R. I examined the dataset, reviewed summary statistics, and visualized the relationship between horsepower and fuel efficiency. The scatter plot shows that cars with higher horsepower generally tend to have lower fuel efficiency.

title: My First Weeks in MDS
text:
Me before MDS: “I’ve got this.”
Me after Week 2: “Who invited Git, Quarto, Bash, Python, R and five deadlines to the same party?” 😭
I knew MDS would be challenging, but I didn’t expect it to hit the gas pedal on day one. Somewhere between orientation and my first assignment, I realized that “I’ll catch up tomorrow” is a dangerous sentence.
The funny part? Every time I think I’ve finally figured something out, the course casually introduces three new things I’ve never heard of before. It’s a constant cycle of confusion, Googling, tiny victories, and celebrating because my terminal finally stopped yelling at me.
Would I choose this chaos again? Absolutely. Ask me again during quiz week… and the answer might depend on how much coffee I’ve had. ☕😄



My first days at UBC.

The dataset contains measurements for different penguin species. The summary statistics provide an overview of the numerical variables, including bill length, bill depth, flipper length, and body mass.

title: Exploring Palmer Penguins with Python
section: Relationship between bill length and flipper length
text:
Relationship between bill length and flipper length
The scatter plot below shows the relationship between bill length and flipper length for different penguin species.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

for species in penguins["species"].unique():
    subset = penguins[penguins["species"] == species]
    plt.scatter(
        subset["bill_length_mm"],
        subset["flipper_length_mm"],
        label=species,
        alpha=0.7
    )

plt.xlabel("Bill length (mm)")
plt.ylabel("Flipper length (mm)")
plt.legend()
plt.show()







Figure 1: Bill length versus flipper length for Palmer Penguins.

title: Exploring Palmer Penguins with Python
text:
Conclusion
In this analysis, I explored the Palmer Penguins dataset using Python. I examined the size of the dataset, generated summary statistics, and visualized the relationship between bill length and flipper length. The scatter plot suggests that different penguin species have distinct physical characteristics, making this dataset useful for exploratory data analysis and visualization.
